key_insight: Water molecules in layered Andersson-Wadsley titanates self-organize into 1D chains that enable highly anisotropic, superionic proton transport.
engineering_relevance: These hydrated titanates could serve as orientation-sensitive proton conductors for solid-state devices where fast room-temperature ion transport is needed.
method: SEM to visualize hydration-dependent 1D patterns and exfoliated surfaces
DFT simulations to resolve ordered water placement and hydrogen bonding
IR spectroscopy and conductivity measurements to link structure with proton transport
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ordered 1D water double chains at low hydration, hydrated (001) surfaces at higher hydration, and room-temperature conductivity up to 3 mS/cm along b in Rb2Ti2O5.
watch_item: The strong conductivity depends on crystal orientation and hydration level, so practical use will require precise control of water content and microstructure.
paper_title: One-dimensional self-organization of water molecules in proton conducting Andersson-Wadsley titanates
